# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`
  (four modes — `sequence` equal-width slots, `duration` with idle gaps
  compressed out, `time` zero-width wall-clock markers, `actual` real gaps;
  three fixed lanes: 0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools),
  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),
  and `ThrottledTrajectorySearchIndex` (full-text; matches are stable
  record ids). `formatters.dart` holds the shared duration/token/throughput
  formatting; `trajectory_preview.dart` the bounded single-line previews;
  `trajectory_export.dart` the whole-snapshot JSON/Markdown exporters the
  header's copy menu uses. Tool records carry `startedAt` (real launch
  time, distinct from the projected position) so the Gantt/actual
  projections plot true spans. Outbound model requests persist for the
  ledger …

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Package browser_ext/ into build/fa-extension.zip (runtime files only:
# manifest, sw/, content/, panel/ — README, dart/ sources, test/, and
# compiled artifacts' side files stay out).
# `--with-app` first builds the Flutter web app (flutter_app/ → build/web) and
# bundles it as browser_ext/app/ so the side panel hosts the full fa app.
# browser_ext/app/ is a build artifact (gitignored, never committed).
# Compiles the embedded Dart agent first when a Dart SDK is available
# (scripts must FAIL LOUDLY on compile errors — CI always builds it).

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Assemble the Office add-in site slice into build/pages/root/outlook/
# (issues #89, #182): manifest, the Flutter web app bundle (outlook/app/ —
# the taskpane IS the fa app), the one-release redirect shim, support /
# privacy pages and icons. Build artifact — never committed. Fail loudly:
# manifest validation errors and flutter build errors abort the build.
# `--dev` rewrites every https://fa1.dev URL to https://localhost:8443
# and validates the REWRITTEN manifest (what will actually ship).
# Runs green on ubuntu-latest and macOS: needs bash + dart + flutter +
# python3 (the app bundle is mandatory now — the pane has no other
# surface).
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

dev=0
for arg in "$@"; do
  case "$arg" in
    --dev) dev=1 ;;
    *) echo "unknown option: $arg (usage: $0 [--dev])" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
done

manifest=office_addin/manifest/outlook.xml
out=build/pages/root/outlook

# --- 1. Assemble + validate the manifest exactly as it will ship. ---
rm -rf "$out"
mkdir -p "$out/icons"
if [ "$dev" -eq 1 ]; then
  sed 's|https://fa1.dev|https://localhost:8443|g' "$manifest" > "$out/manifest.xml"
else
  cp "$manifest" "$out/manifest.xml"
fi
dev_flag=""
if [ "$dev" -eq 1 ]; then dev_flag="--dev"; fi
( cd office_addin/dart \
  && dart pub get >/dev/null \
  && dart run tool/validate_manifest.dart "../../$out/manifest.xml" $dev_flag )

# --- 2. Static pages + icons (index.html is a redirect shim kept one
# release so existing sideloaded manifests land on the app). ---
cp office_addin/web/index.html office_addin/web/privacy.html office_addin/web/support.html "$out/"
cp office_addin/icons/fa-16.png office_addin/icons/fa-32.png office_addin/icons/fa-80.png office_addin/icons/fa-64.png office_addin/icons/fa-128.png "$out/icons/"

# --- 3. The fa web app (flutter_app → outlook/app) — MANDATORY. ---
if ! command -v flutter >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "ERROR: flutter is not installed — cannot build outlook/app/" >&2
  exit 1
fi
echo "building fa web app (flutter build web --release)…"
# --base-href MUST match the taskpane URL: the pane opens
# /outlook/app/index.html directly (manifest 1.2.0.0), so the bundle
# lives at build/pages/root/outlook/app/.
( cd flutter_app && flutter pub get >/dev/null && \
  FLUTTER_WEB_CANVASKIT_URL=./canvaskit/ \
  flutter build web --release --pwa-strategy=none --base-href=/outlook/app/ \
    --dart-define=FA_HOST=office )
rm -rf "$out/app"
mkdir -p "$out/app"
cp -R flutter_app/build/web/. "$out/app/"
# Vendored WASI interpreter assets are mobile-only (#1096 AC3): loaded
# exclusively through WasiSandboxShell (env_factory_io.dart — Android/iOS);
# the web pane compiles env_factory_stub (wasm_run needs dart:ffi) and
# runs python/js/sqlite from cdn.jsdelivr.net (web_interpreters_web.dart).
# ~47MB that never loads in the browser — drop from the bundle.
rm -rf "$out/app/assets/assets/wasm"

# fa1.dev is a hosted page (no extension CSP): CDN scripts are allowed,
# but the canvaskit copy still must mirror the layout the bootstrap
# asks for — same blocks as build_browser_ext.sh.
python3 - <<'PYS'
import glob
for f in glob.glob('flutter_app/build/web/flutter_bootstrap.js') + glob.glob('build/pages/root/outlook/app/flutter_bootstrap.js'):
    t = open(f).read()
    t = t.replace('https://www.gstatic.com/flutter-canvaskit/', './canvaskit/')
    t = t.replace('https:\\/\\/www.gstatic.com\\/flutter-canvaskit\\/', '.\\/canvaskit\\/')
    t = t.replace('"https://www.gstatic.com/flutter-canvaskit"', '"./canvaskit"')
    open(f, 'w').write(t)
PYS
# The engine requests canvaskit under <engineRevision>/chromium/; the
# build lays the copies flat — mirror the layout the bootstrap asks for.
# Extract the FULL engine revision from the bootstrap config — a bounded
# grep like [a-f0-9]{32} silently truncates the 40-char SHA1 and the
# engine then 404s on canvaskit/<rev>/chromium/ (regression).
REV=$(grep -o '"engineRevision":"[a-f0-9]*"' flutter_app/build/web/flutter_bootstrap.js | head -1 | sed 's/.*":"//;s/"//')
if [ -n "$REV" ]; then
  if [ ${#REV} -ne 40 ]; then
    echo "FATAL: engineRevision '$REV' is not 40 hex chars" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  # Copy from the BUILD OUTPUT, never from the bundle copy itself —
  # the rev dir lives inside the bundle copy, so self-copying there
  # recurses into itself (File name too long on the next run).
  mkdir -p "build/pages/root/outlook/app/canvaskit/$REV"
  cp -R "flutter_app/build/web/canvaskit/." "build/pages/root/outlook/app/canvaskit/$REV/"
  for f in canvaskit.js canvaskit.wasm; do
    [ -f "build/pages/root/outlook/app/canvaskit/$REV/chromium/$f" ] || {
      echo "FATAL: canvaskit/$REV/chromium/$f missing after mirror" >&2
      exit 1
    }
  done
  echo "canvaskit mirrored to canvaskit/$REV/chromium/ (verified)"
  # canvaskit dedup (#1096): the engine only requests canvaskit/<rev>/…,
  # the flat top-level copy from build/web is unreachable (~13MB dup).
  find "build/pages/root/outlook/app/canvaskit" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 ! -name "$REV" -exec rm -rf {} +
else
  echo "FATAL: engineRevision not found in flutter_bootstrap.js" >&2
  exit 1
fi

# --- 4. Office host wiring inside the app page (issue #182). ---
# (a) Office.js from the official CDN, BEFORE the flutter bootstrap so
#     Office.initialize/onReady is defined when the app's JsOfficeApi
#     facade calls into it. (b) The pane CSP as a meta tag — pinned
#     without 'unsafe-inline' for scripts: helper code rides blob: URLs
#     (web_interpreters_web.dart); connect-src is open because provider
#     endpoints are user-configured arbitrary origins; script-src allows
#     jsdelivr (quickjs / pyodide / sql.js / webllm / transformers) and
#     appsforoffice.microsoft.com. NOTE: frame-ancestors is NOT
#     enforceable via meta (only via an HTTP header, which GitHub Pages
#     cannot set) — Outlook's own taskpane framing relies on Outlook's
#     sandboxing, documented in docs/outlook-addin.md.
python3 - "$out/app/index.html" <<'PYS'
import re, sys

path = sys.argv[1]
html = open(path).read()

office_script = (
    '<!-- Office.js (official CDN) — the mail bridge the fa app calls '
    '(issue #182). Must precede the flutter bootstrap. -->\n'
    '  <script src="https://appsforoffice.microsoft.com/lib/1/hosted/office.js"></script>\n'
)
csp = (
    '  <!-- Pane CSP (meta-only: GitHub Pages cannot set headers; '
    'frame-ancestors is unenforceable via meta — see docs/outlook-addin.md). -->\n'
    '  <meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy" content="'
    "default-src 'self'; "
    "script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval' blob: "
    'https://appsforoffice.microsoft.com https://cdn.jsdelivr.net; '
    "style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; "
    "img-src 'self' data: blob:; "
    "font-src 'self' data:; "
    "worker-src 'self' blob:; "
    'connect-src * data: blob:; '
    "media-src 'self' blob: data:; "
    "frame-src 'self' blob: data: about:\" />"
)

if 'appsforoffice.microsoft.com' in html:
    print(f'FATAL: {path} already wired (office.js present) — rebuild from a clean bundle')
    sys.exit(1)
html, n_boot = re.subn(
    r'([ \t]*)<script src="flutter_bootstrap\.js"',
    lambda m: m.group(1) + office_script + m.group(1) + '<script src="flutter_bootstrap.js"',
    html, count=1)
html, n_meta = re.subn(r'</head>', csp + '\n</head>', html, count=1)
if n_boot != 1 or n_meta != 1:
    print(f'FATAL: injection anchors not found in {path} (bootstrap={n_boot}, head={n_meta})')
    sys.exit(1)
open(path, 'w').write(html)
print('injected office.js + pane CSP into', path)
PYS

# --- 5. Persistence asset guard (issue #470): the pane must ship the
# fs_store.js tag + file, or every boot loses sessions — assert it, loudly.
python3 scripts/check_embed_assets.py check "$out/app"

echo "bundled fa web app (build/pages/root/outlook/app/)"

echo "assembled $out/:"
find "$out" -type f | sort | while read -r f; do
  printf '%8d  %s\n' "$(wc -c < "$f")" "${f#"$out"/}"
done

The `build_office_addin.sh` script `cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."` to repo root, `out=build/pages/root/outlook`. The new canvaskit dedup uses hardcoded `build/pages/root/outlook/app/canvaskit` which equals `$out/app/canvaskit`. Consistent with existing pre-new-code style: the mirror lines above already hardcode `build/pages/root/outlook/app/canvaskit/$REV`. So the dedup line matches existing style. OK, consistent. (Could use "$out" but matches surrounding code.)

Note one subtle difference vs. build_browser_ext.sh: in the office script, the wasm prune happens BEFORE the canvaskit mirror — fine.

      - name: Package as DMG
        id: package
        env:
          SIGNED: ${{ steps.signing.outputs.signed }}
          PROFILE_EMBEDDED: ${{ steps.signing.outputs.profile_embedded }}
          MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID: ${{ secrets.MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID }}
          VERSION: ${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}
        run: |
          ARCH="${{ matrix.arch }}"
          APP_PATH="flutter_app/build/macos/Build/Products/Release/Fa.app"
          DMG_NAME="fa-macos-${ARCH}-${VERSION}.dmg"

          rm -f fa-macos-*.dmg tmp-fa.dmg
          rm -rf dmg-staging

          echo "Packaging: $APP_PATH → $DMG_NAME (arch: $ARCH)"

          if [ "$SIGNED" = "true" ] && [ -n "$MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID" ]; then
            echo "Signing .app bundle..."

            RESVG_BIN="$APP_PATH/Contents/Resources/resvg"
            if [ -f "$RESVG_BIN" ]; then
              echo "Stripping extended attributes from resvg..."
              xattr -cr "$RESVG_BIN" 2>/dev/null || true
              echo "Signing resvg binary..."
              codesign --force --sign "$MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID" \
                --options runtime \
                --timestamp \
                "$RESVG_BIN"
            fi

            find "$APP_PATH" -type f \( -perm +111 -o -name '*.dylib' \) | while read -r bin; do
              if codesign -dv "$bin" 2>/dev/null | grep -q "$MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID"; then
                continue
              fi
              echo "Signing nested binary: $bin"
              codesign --force --sign "$MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID" \
                --options runtime \
                --timestamp \
                "$bin" 2>/dev/null || true
            done

            if [ "$PROFILE_EMBEDDED" = "true" ] && [ -f "profile.provisionprofile" ]; then
              echo "Embedding provisioning profile..."
              cp profile.provisionprofile "$APP_PATH/Contents/embedded.provisionprofile"
              APP_ID=$(security cms -D -i profile.provisionprofile | plutil -extract Entitlements xml1 -o - - | grep -A 1 'com.apple.application-identifier' | tail -1 | sed 's/.*<string>\(.*\)<\/string>.*/\1/')
              TEAM_ID="${APP_ID%%.*}"
              # Start from Release.entitlements (network client+server, file
              # bookmarks, calendar, contacts, health, homekit, audio input)
              # and inject the provisioning identity keys — do NOT collapse
              # to a sandbox-only dict: the app needs every entitlement the
              # sandbox declares, and dropping them breaks SSO callback
              # servers, file access, and OS-level permission flows in the
              # signed production build.
              cp flutter_app/macos/Runner/Release.entitlements entitlements.plist
              # PlistBuddy handles dotted top-level key names (plutil
              # -insert/-replace treats dots as nested key separators).
              /usr/libexec/PlistBuddy -c "Add :com.apple.application-identifier string $APP_ID" entitlements.plist
              /usr/libexec/PlistBuddy -c "Add :com.apple.developer.team-identifier string $TEAM_ID" entitlements.plist
              # The profile may not grant every *capability* the app declares
              # (e.g. homekit needs a separate App ID capability in the
              # Developer Portal). TestFlight rejects capability entitlements
              # the profile doesn't include ('Invalid Code Signing
              # Entitlements', error 90285).
              #
              # Only com.apple.developer.* keys are profile-gated. The
              # com.apple.security.* sandbox entitlements (network, files,
              # personal-information) are NOT in the profile by design — any
              # sandboxed app may declare them — so they must survive.
              #
              # NOTE: `plutil -extract ... -o -` (stdout form) is not
              # supported on every macOS the runner may have; use real temp
              # files so the extraction can't silently produce nothing.
              security cms -D -i profile.provisionprofile -o profile_decoded.plist
              plutil -extract Entitlements json profile_decoded.plist -o profile_ents.json
              for KEY in $(plutil -convert xml1 entitlements.plist -o - | grep -o '<key>[^<]*</key>' | sed 's/<[^>]*>//g'); do
                case "$KEY" in
                  com.apple.application-identifier|com.apple.developer.team-identifier) continue ;;
                  com.apple.developer.*) ;;
                  *) continue ;; # sandbox + misc entitlements are not profile-gated
                esac
                if ! python3 -c "import json; d=json.load(open('profile_ents.json')); raise SystemExit(0 if '$KEY' in d else 1)"; then
                  echo "Dropping capability not granted by profile: $KEY"
                  /usr/libexec/PlistBuddy -c "Delete :$KEY" entitlements.plist
                fi
              done
              ENTITLEMENTS="entitlements.plist"
            else
              ENTITLEMENTS="flutter_app/macos/Runner/Release.entitlements"
            fi

            codesign_app() {
              codesign --force --deep --sign "$MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID" \
                --options runtime \
                --timestamp \
                --entitlements "$ENTITLEMENTS" \
                "$APP_PATH"
            }

            for attempt in 1 2 3 4 5; do
              if codesign_app; then
                break
              fi
              if [ "$attempt" = "5" ]; then
                echo "codesign failed after $attempt attempts"
                exit 1
              fi
              sleep_seconds=$((attempt * 30))
              echo "codesign failed, retrying in ${sleep_seconds}s (attempt $attempt/5)..."
              sleep "$sleep_seconds"
            done

            echo "Verifying code signature..."
            codesign -vv --deep --strict "$APP_PATH"
            spctl -a -vv "$APP_PATH" 2>/dev/null || true
          fi

          DMG_STAGING="dmg-staging"
          rm -rf "$DMG_STAGING"
          mkdir "$DMG_STAGING"
          cp -R "$APP_PATH" "$DMG_STAGING/"
          ln -s /Applications "$DMG_STAGING/Applications"

          TMP_DMG="tmp-fa.dmg"
          hdiutil create \
            -volname "Fa $VERSION" \
            -srcfolder "$DMG_STAGING" \
            -ov \
            -format UDRW \
            "$TMP_DMG"

          hdiutil convert "$TMP_DMG" -format UDZO -o "$DMG_NAME"
          rm -f "$TMP_DMG"
          rm -rf "$DMG_STAGING"

          echo "dmg_name=$DMG_NAME" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

          ZIP_NAME="fa-macos-${ARCH}-${VERSION}-mac.zip"
          echo "Packaging ZIP for auto-update: $ZIP_NAME"
          ditto -c -k --sequesterRsrc --keepParent "$APP_PATH" "$ZIP_NAME"
          SHA512=$(openssl dgst -sha512 -binary "$ZIP_NAME" | openssl base64 -A)
          SIZE=$(stat -f%z "$ZIP_NAME")
          MANIFEST_ARCH="$ARCH"
          if [ "$MANIFEST_ARCH" = "x86_64" ]; then
            MANIFEST_ARCH="x64"
          fi
          MANIFEST_NAME="latest-mac-${MANIFEST_ARCH}.yml"
          RELEASE_DATE=$(date -u +"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.000Z")
          printf '%s\n' \
            "version: ${VERSION}" \
            "files:" \
            "  - url: ${ZIP_NAME}" \
            "    sha512: ${SHA512}" \
            "    size: ${SIZE}" \
            "    arch: ${MANIFEST_ARCH}" \
            "path: ${ZIP_NAME}" \
            "sha512: ${SHA512}" \
            "releaseDate: '${RELEASE_DATE}'" \
            > "$MANIFEST_NAME"
          echo "zip_name=$ZIP_NAME" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "manifest_name=$MANIFEST_NAME" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

      # AC1 (#1096): per-entry uncompressed size table + +5% budget gate on
      # the shipped mac zip (auto-update channel). arm64 baseline is
      # committed (v1.0.493); other arches self-seed via --init-if-missing
      # on their next release run — commit the printed manifest to arm.

        run: |
          MANIFEST_ARCH="$MATRIX_ARCH"
          [ "$MANIFEST_ARCH" = "x86_64" ] && MANIFEST_ARCH="x64"
          python3 scripts/size_manifest.py check "${{ steps.package.outputs.zip_name }…

If the gate fails, the artifacts aren't uploaded — good gating for artifact upload, but note: for `create_release == 'true'`, there are separate release jobs (release-macos at 915, release-extension at 854) that re-attach assets from uploaded artifacts. The packaging step uses `ARCH="${{ matrix.arch }}"` and does the same x86_64→x64 mapping for MANIFEST_ARCH. So matrix.arch ∈ {arm64, x86_64}. Baselines: `fa-macos-arm64.tsv` (committed), `fa-macos-x64.tsv` (self-seeds on first x86_64 release run). OK.

So gate has the old shape; the mac zip will still ship the same shape in this slice, so the per-line gate is active for the mac zip from day one. Only the extension zip's baseline is the uncut v1.0.493, whose first gated run shrinks massively (passes), but until re-seed the ratchet is loose (TOTAL budget +5% of the OLD inflated total; new-line threshold 5% of old total = ~8.6MB for the panel). Actually wait, there's a subtlety about TOTAL: after the cut lands, TOTAL is 55% smaller. TOTAL growth budget = +5% of the OLD (171MB) total = +8.5MB of headroom. So up to 8.5MB of new junk could ride in without failing TOTAL, as long as no single new line exceeds 8.6MB and no baseline line grows >5%. Until the baseline is re-seeded to the cut shape. The PR description itself says "The first gated release lands the new shape in the log; any regrowth beyond it fails." — imprecise but the tool prints "improvements" clearly. So the headline risks ARE caught. The gap is only for smaller dead weight. Downgrade to SUGGESTION? Hmm. The gate semantics: "a NEW line heavier than 5% of the baseline TOTAL fails — catches a dropped interpreter sneaking back in". That claim holds. The TOTAL +5% against stale baseline is ~8.6MB headroom. I'll file a SUGGESTION recommending re-seeding baselines immediately after the first cut release (the workflow comment for new arches already instructs committing seeded manifests; a note in the PR to re-seed fa-extension/fa-macos baselines after slice-2 cuts would tighten the ratchet). For the extension gate there's no such self-seed (no --init-if-missing) — baseline committed. OK.

That's a ratchet that requires manual follow-up; acceptable, documented. name: Pages

# Builds the Flutter web demo (flutter_app) into site/app and
# deploys the static landing (site/) to GitHub Pages. Pages source must be
# set to "GitHub Actions" in the repo settings.
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'site/**'
      - 'flutter_app/**'
      - 'packages/**'
      - 'lib/**'
      - 'vendor/**'
      - 'browser_ext/**'
      - 'scripts/build_browser_ext.sh'
      - 'office_addin/**'
      - 'scripts/build_office_addin.sh'
      - '.github/workflows/pages.yml'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

# One deploy at a time; queued runs must not be cancelled mid-deploy.
concurrency:
  group: pages
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  build:
    name: Build landing + web demo
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Ceiling for the daily website watcher's budget arithmetic (#351):
    # flutter web build + extension dart2js + add-in build + a Playwright
    # chromium boot smoke; historically ~15m, 45m is the slow-day bound.
    timeout-minutes: 45
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: stable

      - name: Example app pub get
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: flutter pub get

      # .env is gitignored but declared as a Flutter asset (flutter_dotenv);
      # the build fails without it.
      - name: Placeholder .env for the example app
        run: touch [REDACTED:Credential File]

      # firebase_options.dart is gitignored too (real keys stay local). The
      # web build needs the file to compile: copy the tracked placeholder —
      # main.dart skips Firebase init for YOUR_* values, so the demo runs
      # without Analytics (as it always has).
      - name: Placeholder firebase_options.dart for the example app
        run: >-
          cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart
          flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      - name: Build web demo
        working-directory: flutter_app
        id: web_build
        run: >-
          flutter build web --release
          --base-href /app/
          --output ../build/pages/app

      # The vendored WASI interpreter assets are mobile-only (#1096 AC3):
      # assets/wasm/* loads exclusively through WasiSandboxShell
      # (env_factory_io.dart — Android/iOS); the web build compiles
      # env_factory_stub (wasm_run needs dart:ffi) and runs python/js/
      # sqlite from cdn.jsdelivr.net (web_interpreters_web.dart). ~47MB
      # of dead weight in the deploy root — prune post-build, flags
      # untouched. The extension/office panel builds prune the same set
      # inside their packaging scripts.
      - name: Prune mobile-only wasm interpreter assets (#1096 AC3)
        run: rm -rf build/pages/app/assets/assets/wasm

      # The Chrome extension ships on the site too (download + load
      # unpacked): dart2js the SW agent and zip it — flutter is already on
      # PATH here and the script's --with-app embeds the same web build.
      - name: Build Chrome extension
        run: |
          dart pub get
          cd browser_ext/dart && dart pub get && cd ../..
          bash scripts/build_browser_ext.sh --with-app

      # The Office add-in ships on the site too (sideload from
      # fa1.dev/outlook/manifest.xml): the script validates the manifest,
      # builds the fa web app with the office host flag (the pane IS the
      # app, outlook/app/) and assembles build/pages/root/outlook/ in
      # place — BEFORE the assemble step, so the artifact dir persists
      # into the upload.
      - name: Build Office add-in
        run: |
          cd office_addin/dart && dart pub get && cd ../..
          bash scripts/build_office_addin.sh

      - name: Assemble Pages artifact
        run: |
          mkdir -p build/pages/root
          cp -R site/. build/pages/root/
          # The App Store frames page (issue #691): the images are the
          # COMMITTED GOLDENS, copied at deploy — never hand-copied PNGs,
          # so the site assets cannot drift from the store assets (the
          # page↔golden set is pinned by test/site/appstore_assets_test.dart).
          mkdir -p build/pages/root/app-store/img
          cp flutter_app/test/goldens/store/en/ios/*.png build/pages/root/app-store/img/
          # Only copy the web app if it built successfully.
          if [ -d build/pages/app ]; then
            cp -R build/pages/app build/pages/root/app
          fi
          # The extension zip lives under /extension/ on fa1.dev.
          if [ -f build/fa-extension.zip ]; then
            mkdir -p build/pages/root/extension
            cp build/fa-extension.zip build/pages/root/extension/fa-extension.zip
          fi

      - name: Cache-bust static assets
        if: steps.web_build.outcome == 'success'
        env:
          BUILD_ID: ${{ github.sha }}
        run: |
          # Bust the Flutter demo app's entry scripts so browsers never load a
          # stale flutter_bootstrap.js / helper bundle after a new deploy.
          sed -i -E 's|src="([^\"]+)"|src="\1?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'"|g' build/pages/app/index.html
          # Bust the landing page's own CSS/JS and the demo-app iframe/link.
          sed -i -E 's|href="styles\.css"|href="styles.css?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'"|g' build/pages/root/index.html
          sed -i -E 's|src="main\.js" defer|src="main.js?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'" defer|g' build/pages/root/index.html
          sed -i -E 's|src="\./app/"|src="./app/index.html?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'"|g' build/pages/root/index.html
          sed -i -E 's|href="\./app/" target="_blank"|href="./app/index.html?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'" target="_blank"|g' build/pages/root/index.html

      - name: Size manifest + budget gate (#1096 AC1)
        run: |
          # Per-entry uncompressed size table + +5% budget per line (issue
          # inventory format). First run seeds web-app.tsv in the workspace
          # (--init-if-missing) — commit it to arm the web gate; the
          # extension zip gate is armed by the committed release baseline
          # (the release zip itself is gated in build-macos.yml).
          python3 scripts/size_manifest.py check build/pages/app \
            --baseline scripts/size_budget/web-app.tsv --init-if-missing
          if [ -d build/pages/root/outlook/app ]; then
            python3 scripts/size_manifest.py check build/pages/root/outlook/app \
              --baseline scripts/size_budget/outlook-app.tsv --init-if-missing
          fi

      - uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@fc324d3547104276b827a68afc52ff2a11cc49c9 # v5.0.0
        with:
          path: build/pages/root

      # Gate the deploy on a real-browser boot smoke: serve the assembled
      # artifact and drive headless Chromium — the app must mount and run
      # Dart main() with zero console errors. Dart tests cannot catch
      # runtime JS-interop crashes (once shipped: the extension probe threw
      # a null-check on every normal page); this can and did.
      - name: Web boot smoke (headless Chromium)
        working-directory: build/pages/root
        run: |
          python3 -m http.server 8788 --bind 127.0.0.1 >/dev/null 2>&1 &
          SERVER_PID=$!
          trap 'kill $SERVER_PID 2>/dev/null || true' EXIT
          cd "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          npm init -y >/dev/null
          npm i --no-fund --no-audit playwright@1.49.1 >/dev/null
          npx playwright install chromium --with-deps >/dev/null
          node scripts/web_boot_smoke.mjs http://127.0.0.1:8788/app/

    name: Deploy to GitHub Pages
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Ceiling for the daily website watcher's budget arithmetic (#351).
    timeout-minutes: 15
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:
      - id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@368f82528645a54fb793d4d04e342629a3f51346 # v5.0.1

runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Ceiling for the daily cli watcher's budget arithmetic (#351).
    timeout-minutes: 30
    if: inputs.create_release == 'true'
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: stable

      - name: dart pub get (root)
        run: dart pub get

      # browser_ext/dart is a separate package (path dep on this root), so
      # its pub get must follow the root's — same as browser-ext.yml.
      - name: dart pub get (browser_ext/dart)
        run: cd browser_ext/dart && dart pub get

      # Full artifact: SW agent (dart2js) + the Flutter panel app embedded,
      # exactly what "Load unpacked" expects. --clobber keeps the stable
      # asset name fa-extension.zip pointing at the newest build (the
      # landing page links it directly).
      - name: Build extension zip
        run: bash scripts/build_browser_ext.sh --with-app

      # AC1 (#1096): per-entry uncompressed size table + +5% budget gate
      # against the committed v1.0.493 release baseline. Shrink passes;
      # growth (e.g. a dropped interpreter re-added) fails the release.
      - name: Size manifest + budget gate (fa-extension.zip)
        run: python3 scripts/size_manifest.py check build/fa-extension.zip --baseline scripts/size_budget/fa-extension.tsv

      - name: Upload extension to the release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ needs.version.outputs.tag }}
        run: |

Selftest passes 7/7. Good.

Now the release-extension job: has checkout, builds the extension, gates against the committed baseline, then uploads. Gate failure blocks upload — good. Note: the release-extension job uses `subosito/flutter-action` with `channel: stable` — floating stable. A stable Flutter bump changes main.dart.js size and engineRevision — canvaskit rev churn trips NEW-line/removed-lines, main.dart.js could shift >5%? A Flutter upgrade could fail the release gate — that's by design ("re-growth must be a conscious ack") and the escape hatch is documented (re-seed). OK.

Now let me verify remaining risk areas:

1. The `browser-ext.yml` path filter claim ("browser-ext.yml path-filters scripts/build_browser_ext.sh") — check the workflow file name and paths filter.

2. web_boot_smoke.mjs — exists (scripts/web_boot_smoke.mjs — yes, saw it in ls).

3. The mac zip gate placement — verified at line 609, before "Upload macOS artifacts" (line 711). Good. But wait — is there anything between the gate and the upload that would publish the zip earlier (e.g. auto-update manifest merge in release-macos job is separate)? release-macos job (line 915) merges latest-mac manifest and uploads to release — it `needs` the build job? Let me check `needs:` for release-macos. If release-macos downloads artifacts produced by the build job, a gate failure in the build job blocks the release. The "Upload macOS artifacts" step (line 711) is in the build job after the gate — so a failing gate fails the build job → no artifact → release job fails/skips. Good.

4. Now a deeper check on the mac zip gate: `python3 scripts/size_manifest.py check "${{ steps.package.outputs.zip_name }}"` — zip_name is set in the package step. But NOTE: if signing is skipped (SIGNED != true), the package step still runs and sets zip_name. OK. But what if the `package` step FAILS midway (e.g. hdiutil error)? Then zip_name output may be empty → gate step runs `check ""` → iter_sizes(Path("")) → not file, not dir → SystemExit "artifact not found" exit... SystemExit with a string message → exit code 1. Job already failed at package step. Fine.

5. Check the matrix arch values in build-macos.yml.

6. Check the docstring TOTAL-format mismatch — confirmed mismatch: docstring says `TOTAL\t<total_bytes>`; write_baseline emits `<total>\tTOTAL`; load_baseline expects `<size>\t<name>`. The committed baselines use `<size>\t<name>`. So only the docstring is wrong. SUGGESTION.

7. Check NEW_LINE_SHARE edge: `cur > NEW_LINE_SHARE * base_total` — strict >. Fine.

8. One more check — the `check` for directory artifact in pages.yml runs on `build/pages/app` AFTER cache-bust (sed mutated index.html — trivial size change) — consistent for future runs (every run cache-busts, same shape). OK.

9. pages.yml gate: `--init-if-missing` on BOTH checks unconditionally — even AFTER baselines get committed, the flag stays. Is that a problem? With a committed baseline present, `--init-if-missing` is a no-op (file exists → normal compare). The escape hatch semantics: "re-run locally with the same artifact and --init-if-missing (it rewrites the baseline)". Wait — the docstring says `--init-if-missing: no baseline file yet -> write it and pass` — it only seeds when MISSING. The CLI escape-hatch note says "re-run locally with the same artifact and --init-if-missing (it rewrites the baseline)" — that's WRONG: if the baseline EXISTS, --init-if-missing does NOT rewrite it; the gate compares. To re-seed an existing baseline you'd delete the file first, or use --manifest-out. The error message also says: "intentional growth? re-seed with: python3 scripts/size_manifest.py check <artifact> --baseline {baseline_path} --init-if-missing" — following that instruction verbatim does NOT re-seed (baseline exists → still fails). That's a real UX/correctness bug in the tool's own escape-hatch instructions: the documented re-seed path doesn't work without deleting the baseline first. I'd rate IMPORTANT (the tool's documented escape hatch misleads; the CI failure message tells the operator to run a command that won't fix the problem). Actually — wait, let me re-check: `if not baseline_path.exists(): if init_if_missing: write_baseline...`. Yes — only when missing. The docstring: "CI escape hatch for intentional growth: re-run locally with the same artifact and `--init-if-missing` (it rewrites the baseline) and commit it." — incorrect. And the failure hint repeats it. The operator following the hint gets the same failure. The workaround: `--manifest-out <baseline_path>` DOES overwrite the baseline unconditionally (write_baseline at top of check). So the correct hint should be `--manifest-out`. Definitely a finding — IMPORTANT (workflow escape hatch broken as documented; operator confusion during an incident, though no data loss).

Severity call: It doesn't break the build; it makes the documented recovery path fail. IMPORTANT feels right (real correctness issue in the new tooling's contract, immediately visible on first intentional growth).

10. Another look at the mac-gate `[ ... ] && MANIFEST_ARCH="x64"` under GitHub's default shell (bash -e? Actually default shell for run on non-Windows: `bash -e {0}`). As established, `false && x` doesn't trip -e. Verified behavior. Not a bug. But note the packaging step above ALREADY computes MANIFEST_ARCH with the same mapping and outputs... `manifest_name=latest-mac-${MANIFEST_ARCH}.yml` — the arch is derivable from `steps.package.outputs.manifest_name` (latest-mac-x64.yml) — could parse instead of duplicating; but the current approach via env is fine and actually safer against quoting. Not worth a comment beyond a nit — skip.

The PR consciously keeps scripts self-contained (pages.yml prune is a one-liner because the workflow builds the demo app without the scripts). This is acceptable; could suggest a shared helper (scripts/prune_web_bundle.sh) to keep the cuts consistent when the wasm set changes (e.g. slice 2 removing more assets). The workflow comment cross-references. SUGGESTION.

12. IMPORTANT candidate — **gate hole in pages.yml: the extension zip shipped on the site (`build/pages/root/extension/fa-extension.zip`) is never gated in pages.yml**. The release zip IS gated in build-macos.yml. Two producers of the same asset name; only one gated. Cheap fix: add a third check line in pages.yml for build/fa-extension.zip against scripts/size_budget/fa-extension.tsv (no --init-if-missing needed; baseline committed). Worth SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT? The site zip feeding users could regrow 35MB silently while the release gate stays green. But both are built by the same script with the same cuts; the risk is a flutter stable bump (floating channel) changing behavior — which WOULD be caught in the release job (also floating stable). Hmm, both float stable — mostly same shape. I'll make it a SUGGESTION.

13. **MIN_BYTES floor vs the gate's core promise**: "a NEW line heavier than 5% of the baseline TOTAL fails — catches a dropped interpreter sneaking back in". With baseline TOTAL = 175MB (extension), threshold = 8.76MB. python.wasm 30MB → caught. canvaskit rev (37MB in one dir = multiple lines: canvaskit.wasm 7.2MB, chromium/canvaskit.wasm 5.4MB...) — if the DEDUP regressed (flat copy re-appearing), the re-appearing flat lines are each ≤ ~7.3MB < 8.76MB → NONE of them individually trips the NEW-line check! The CI failure message and the docstring tell the operator to fix an intentional-growth failure with:

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review"] O2["Write outputs/pr_review_general.md — brief general PR comment (1-2 paragraphs max)"] O3["Write ou…

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1110
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1110
- **Title**: feat(#1096): release size manifest gate + unambiguous extension/web cuts (slice 1)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1096` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 7
- **Additions**: +425
- **Deletions**: -0
- **Created**: 2026-09-30T12:01:01Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-30T12:18:27Z

## PR Description

Part of #1096 — slice 1 (additive, non-controversial cuts + the size-budget gate). Owner-decision items are NOT touched (list at the bottom).

## What ships

### AC1 — CI size manifest + budget gate
- `scripts/size_manifest.py` — `emit` (per-entry uncompressed size table, issue-inventory format), `check` (gate: any baseline line or TOTAL growing beyond +5% fails; a NEW line heavier than 5% of the baseline TOTAL fails — catches a dropped interpreter sneaking back in; `--init-if-missing` ratchet bootstrap for artifacts with no baseline yet), `selftest` (7 synthetic assertions — all pass locally).
- Committed baselines generated from the real **v1.0.493 release artifacts**: `scripts/size_budget/fa-extension.tsv`, `scripts/size_budget/fa-macos-arm64.tsv` (other arches / web root self-seed on their next CI run via `--init-if-missing`).
- Wired into: `build-macos.yml` (extension release zip + mac auto-update zip, before upload), `pages.yml` (web deploy root). Release-shaped artifacts only; the browser-ext.yml scaffold zip stays as-is.

### AC2 — extension cuts (no owner decision needed)
`scripts/build_browser_ext.sh` now, after bundling the panel app:
1. **canvaskit dedup** — keeps only `panel/app/canvaskit/<engineRevision>/` (the verified-complete mirror the bootstrap actually requests), drops the flat top-level copy from `build/web`.
2. **dead python runtime dropped (OQ2 resolved: pyodide is the live one)** — `panel/app/assets/assets/wasm/` removed from the panel bundle. Execution-path evidence:
   - Every `rootBundle.load('assets/wasm/…')` lives in `WasiSandboxShell` (`flutter_app/lib/sandbox/wasm_shell.dart`), reachable only via `env_factory_io.dart` whose factory guards `Platform.isAndroid || Platform.isIOS` (`env_factory_io.dart:40-43`). The web panel compiles `env_factory_stub` instead (`env_factory.dart` conditional export; `package:wasm_run` imports `dart:ffi`, uncompilable for browsers).
   - The extension's LIVE interpreter is the vendored **pyodide** in `vendor/interpreters/` loaded by `offscreen/interpreters.js`, wired through the `run_script` tool in the SW agent (current source: "Run user scripts in the bundled Python/JavaScript interpreters… offscreen.html") — kept untouched.

### AC3 — web deploy stops shipping the mobile-only interpreters
- `pages.yml` prunes `build/pages/app/assets/assets/wasm` right after `flutter build web` (flags untouched — this is a post-build prune).
- `scripts/build_office_addin.sh` gets the identical prune + canvaskit dedup (same web-build shape in the same deploy root).
- CDN evidence: the web sandbox runs python/js/sqlite from cdn.jsdelivr.net (`web_interpreters_web.dart`: quickjs-emscripten 0.31.0, pyodide v0.26.4, sql.js 1.14.1; documented in `memory_shell.dart`).

## Proof (real artifacts, v1.0.493 release zip vs cut zip)

| metric | before | after | saved |
|---|---|---|---|
| fa-extension.zip (compressed) | 61.9 MB (64,900,856 B) | 26.9 MB (28,246,450 B) | **35.0 MB (−56%)** |
| panel/ unpacked total | 171,484 KB | 76,348 KB | **95,136 KB (−55.5%)** |
| — `panel/app/assets/assets/wasm/` | 58,132 KB | 0 | 58,132 KB |
| — `panel/app/canvaskit/` | 74,008 KB | 37,004 KB (rev subtree only) | 37,004 KB |

Method: downloaded `fa-extension.zip` from the v1.0.493 release, unzipped, applied exactly the two cuts the script makes (`rm -rf panel/app/assets/assets/wasm` + `find canvaskit -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 ! -name <rev> -exec rm -rf`), rezipped with the script's own zip invocation.
(A local `flutter build web` was not possible on this host — the Flutter SDK dir is not writable here (`update_engine_version.sh: Operation not permitted`) — so the released artifact doubles as the locally-built one; the cuts are pure packaging-file removals, identical either way.)

Gate proof on these artifacts:
- cut zip vs committed v1.0.493 baseline: **PASS** (`TOTAL −55.5%`, shrink-only). The first gated release lands the new shape in the log; any regrowth beyond it fails.
- tampered zip (main.dart.js inflated +10.8%): **FAIL** — `GREW +10.8% panel/app/main.dart.js 11427838 -> 12656638`, exit 1.
- `python3 scripts/size_manifest.py selftest`: 7/7 pass.

### REG-1 (extension still opens)
- **Forensic**: zero references to the removed files in the shipped bundle — `grep -r 'assets/wasm'` over `panel/app/**/*.js|html|json` (incl. `main.dart.js`, `flutter_bootstrap.js`) = **0 hits**; flat-canvaskit refs (`canvaskit/canvaskit|skwasm|chromium|webparagraph`) = **0 hits** (engine only requests `canvaskit/<rev>/chromium/…`); file-set diff `canvaskit/` vs `canvaskit/<rev>/`: 18 flat-layout files existed only outside the rev subtree, **0 files only inside it** — the kept rev copy is a superset.
- **CWS shape guard** on the cut zip: OK — single root manifest.json (MV3), 138 entries, icons present, no junk.
- **Script end-to-end**: `build_browser_ext.sh` (scaffold path) runs green — manifest validation, vendored interpreters, dart2js agent, zip, CWS guard.
- **Real-browser**: headless-Chrome integration suite (`dart test test/browser_ext/ -j 1 --tags integration`) and a direct Chromium boot of the cut panel were attempted locally on Chrome for Testing 154 — **this sandboxed host cannot render pages**: Chromium's seatbelt init fails (`sandbox initialization failed: Operation not permitted`), the GPU process aborts (`GPU process isn't usable. Goodbye.`, exit 133), and with the sandbox disabled the page load event never fires (dump-dom starves; the driver suite then fails 15/18 on DevTools `SocketException: connection refused` / 35s CDP timeouts — all launch-plumbing, zero content assertions reached). Same EPERM class as the known host PTY constraint. The real-browser proof therefore runs in CI, which this PR triggers automatically: browser-ext.yml path-filters `scripts/build_browser_ext.sh` (headless Chrome suite + playwright e2e), and pages.yml runs the web boot smoke (flutter-view mounts + `[fah] starting runApp`, zero console errors).

### Bonus finding for slice 2 (not touched here)
The mac zip baseline shows the same mobile-only set riding along: `Fa.app/.../flutter_assets/assets/wasm/python.wasm` (29 MB) + friends ≈ 47 MB, and `wasm_run_flutter.framework` = 27.1 MB — that's the OQ1/AC4 cut with owner sign-off. Also `canvaskit/<rev>/` still mirrors the flat layout *inside* the rev dir (26.3 MB of `canvaskit.js/wasm`, `skwasm*`, `wimp*` at rev root) — reachable only if the engine ever requests the non-`chromium/` variant; needs a network trace before cutting, so left alone.

## OQ1 verification — `wasm_run_flutter` on macOS is NOT load-bearing (removal = slice 2, owner sign-off)
- `env_factory_io.dart:40-43`: the WASI sandbox shell (`WasiSandboxShell`) is instantiated **only** on Android/iOS; every other platform gets `createDesktopEnv()` (host `Process` shell). macOS never builds it.
- macOS boot *does* register the runtime best-effort (`app_boot.dart:215` → `wasm_setup_io.dart` `WasmRunLibrary.setUp`) — but no macOS code path ever compiles a module (the only module consumers are the mobile shell and the web stub pair).
- Cost: `Fa.app/Contents/Frameworks/wasm_run_flutter.framework` = **27,147,248 bytes** in the shipped v1.0.493 mac zip, vendored by CI (`build-macos.yml` WasmRun.xcframework restore step).
- Documented here per slice 1 scope; the actual macOS target change is GH-2 / slice 2.

## Owner-pending (explicitly NOT implemented in this slice)
- iOS lite flavor vs accept-35MB (AC5) — on-device stack decision.
- On-device LLM stack cuts, direction 1 (LiteRT/Gemma frameworks, 35 MB iOS / 45 MB macOS).
- `--wasm` (skwasm) spike (OQ3) + other web build flags — untouched here; flags unchanged.
- `App.framework` code-size audit, direction 6.
- macOS `wasm_run_flutter.framework` + ma…

    "summary": "feat(#1096): release size manifest gate + unambiguous extension/web cuts (slice 1)",
    "description": "Part of #1096 — slice 1 (additive, non-controversial cuts + the size-budget gate). Owner-decision items are NOT touched (list at the bottom).

## What ships

### AC1 — CI size manifest + budget gate
- `scripts/size_manifest.py` — `emit` (per-entry uncompressed size table, issue-inventory format), `check` (gate: any baseline line or TOTAL growing beyond +5% fails; a NEW line heavier than 5% of the baseline TOTAL fails — catches a dropped interpreter sneaking back in; `--init-if-missing` ratchet bootstrap for artifacts with no baseline yet), `selftest` (7 synthetic assertions — all pass locally).
- Committed baselines generated from the real **v1.0.493 release artifacts**: `scripts/size_budget/fa-extension.tsv`, `scripts/size_budget/fa-macos-arm64.tsv` (other arches / web root self-seed on their next CI run via `--init-if-missing`).
- Wired into: `build-macos.yml` (extension release zip + mac auto-update zip, before upload), `pages.yml` (web deploy root). Release-shaped artifacts only; the browser-ext.yml scaffold zip stays as-is.

### AC2 — extension cuts (no owner decision needed)
`scripts/build_browser_ext.sh` now, after bundling the panel app:
1. **canvaskit dedup** — keeps only `panel/app/canvaskit/<engineRevision>/` (the verified-complete mirror the bootstrap actually requests), drops the flat top-level copy from `build/web`.
2. **dead python runtime dropped (OQ2 resolved: pyodide is the live one)** — `panel/app/assets/assets/wasm/` removed from the panel bundle. Execution-path evidence:
   - Every `rootBundle.load('assets/wasm/…')` lives in `WasiSandboxShell` (`flutter_app/lib/sandbox/wasm_shell.dart`), reachable only via `env_factory_io.dart` whose factory guards `Platform.isAndroid || Platform.isIOS` (`env_factory_io.dart:40-43`). The web panel compiles `env_factory_stub` instead (`env_factory.dart` conditional export; `package:wasm_run` imports `dart:ffi`, uncompilable for browsers).
   - The extension's LIVE interpreter is the vendored **pyodide** in `vendor/interpreters/` loaded by `offscreen/interpreters.js`, wired through the `run_script` tool in the SW agent (current source: "Run user scripts in the bundled Python/JavaScript interpreters… offscreen.html") — kept untouched.

### AC3 — web deploy stops shipping the mobile-only interpreters
- `pages.yml` prunes `build/pages/app/assets/assets/wasm` right after `flutter build web` (flags untouched — this is a post-build prune).
- `scripts/build_office_addin.sh` gets the identical prune + canvaskit dedup (same web-build shape in the same deploy root).
- CDN evidence: the web sandbox runs python/js/sqlite from cdn.jsdelivr.net (`web_interpreters_web.dart`: quickjs-emscripten 0.31.0, pyodide v0.26.4, sql.js 1.14.1; documented in `memory_shell.dart`).

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Per-artifact uncompressed size manifest + budget gate (#1096 AC1).
+
+Emits the per-entry uncompressed size table (the issue's inventory format)
+for a shipped artifact and fails the build when any tracked line regresses
+beyond the budget (default +5%).
+
+Usage:
+  size_manifest.py emit   <artifact> [--min-bytes N]        # TSV to stdout
+  size_manifest.py check  <artifact> --baseline FILE
+                          [--budget-pct 5] [--init-if-missing]
+                          [--manifest-out FILE]
+  size_manifest.py selftest
+
+`<artifact>` is a zip-family file (.zip/.ipa/.aab — uncompressed entry sizes
+via zipfile) or a directory (tree of file sizes, for the web deploy root).
+
+Manifest format (TSV, path-sorted, stable for diffs):
+  <uncompressed_bytes>\t<path>
+  TOTAL\t<total_bytes>            (always last)
+
+Gate semantics (`check`):
+  - growth > budget%% on any baseline line or on TOTAL  -> FAIL
+  - NEW line heavier than 5%% of the baseline TOTAL     -> FAIL
+    (catches re-adding removed weight, e.g. a dropped interpreter coming
+    back; canvaskit rev-dir churn on Flutter upgrades trips this too —
+    that is by design: re-growth must be a conscious ack)
+  - removed lines are improvements, reported only
+  - --init-if-missing: no baseline file yet -> write it and pass with a
+    loud notice (ratchet bootstrap; commit the file to arm the gate)
+
+CI escape hatch for intentional growth: re-run locally with the same
+artifact and `--init-if-missing` (it rewrites the baseline) and commit it.
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import sys
+import zipfile
+from pathlib import Path
+
+# Per-line tracking floor: smaller files are noise (thousands of them
+# jitter by whole percentages); the TOTAL line covers their aggregate.
+MIN_BYTES = 64 * 1024
+# A brand-new tracked line heavier than this share of the old TOTAL is
+# re-growth, not rounding — fail it.
+NEW_LINE_SHARE = 0.05
+
+
+def iter_sizes(artifact: Path):
+    """Yield (path, uncompressed_bytes) for every file in the artifact."""
+    if artifact.is_file():
+        # zip-family: .zip / .ipa / .aab / .apk
+        with zipfile.ZipFile(artifact) as zf:
+            for info in zf.infolist():
+                if info.is_dir():
+                    continue
+                yield info.filename.replace("\t", " "), info.file_size
+        return
+    if artifact.is_dir():
+        for p in sorted(artifact.rglob("*")):
+            if p.is_file() and not p.is_symlink():
+                yield p.relative_to(artifact).as_posix().replace("\t", " "), p.stat().st_size
+        return
+    raise SystemExit(f"size_manifest: artifact not found: {artifact}")
+
+
+def build_manifest(artifact: Path, min_bytes: int) -> "dict[str, int]":
+    sizes = dict(iter_sizes(artifact))
+    manifest = {p: n for p, n in sizes.items() if n >= min_bytes}
+    manifest["TOTAL"] = sum(sizes.values())
+    return manifest
+
+
+def fmt_table(manifest: "dict[str, int]") -> str:
+    width = max((len(p) for p in manifest), default=5)
+    lines = [f"{manifest[p]:>12}  {p.ljust(width)}" for p in sorted(manifest) if p != "TOTAL"]
+    lines.append("-" * (width + 14))
+    lines.append(f"{manifest['TOTAL']:>12}  TOTAL")
+    return "\n".join(lines)
+
+
+def load_baseline(path: Path) -> "dict[str, int]":
+    baseline = {}
+    for line in path.read_text().splitlines():
+        if not line.strip():
+            continue
+        size, _, name = line.partition("\t")
+        baseline[name] = int(size)
+    if "TOTAL" not in baseline:
+        raise SystemExit(f"size_manifest: baseline {path} has no TOTAL line")
+    return baseline
+
+
+def write_baseline(path: Path, manifest: "dict[str, int]") -> None:
+    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    lines = [f"{manifest[p]}\t{p}" for p in sorted(manifest)]
+    path.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
+
+
+def check(artifact: Path, baseline_path: Path, budget_pct: float,
+          init_if_missing: bool, manifest_out=None) -> int:
+    manifest = build_manifest(artifact, MIN_BYTES)
+    if manifest_out:
+        write_baseline(manifest_out, manifest)
+
+    if not baseline_path.exists():
+        if init_if_missing:
+            write_baseline(baseline_path, manifest)
+            print(f"::notice::size_manifest: baseline initialized from this "
+                  f"artifact — COMMIT {baseline_path} to arm the gate")
+            print(fmt_table(manifest))
+            return 0
+        print(f"::error::size_manifest: baseline {baseline_path} missing "
+              f"(run with --init-if-missing to seed it)")
+        return 2
+
+    baseline = load_baseline(baseline_path)
+    base_total = baseline["TOTAL"]
+    failures = []
+    grew, shrank, new, removed = [], [], [], []
+
+    for name in sorted(set(baseline) | set(manifest)):
+        if name == "TOTAL":
+            continue
+        old, cur = baseline.get(name), manifest.get(name)
+        if old is None and cur is not None:
+            new.append((name, cur))
+        elif cur is None:
+            removed.append((name, old))
+        elif cur > old:
+            grew.append((name, old, cur))
+        elif cur < old:
+            shrank.append((name, old, cur))
+
+    for name, old, cur in grew:
+        pct = (cur - old) / old * 100 if old else float("inf")
+        if pct > budget_pct:
+            failures.append(f"  GREW    +{pct:6.1f}%  {name}  {old} -> {cur}")
+    total_pct = (manifest["TOTAL"] - base_total) / base_total * 100 if base_total else 0.0
+    if total_pct > budget_pct:
+        failures.append(f"  TOTAL   +{total_pct:6.1f}%  {base_total} -> {manifest['TOTAL']}")
+    for name, cur in new:
+        if cur > NEW_LINE_SHARE * base_total:
+            failures.append(f"  NEW     {'':>8}  {name}  {cur} bytes "
+                            f"(> {NEW_LINE_SHARE:.0%} of baseline TOTAL)")
+
+    print(f"size manifest: {artifact}  (budget: +{budget_pct}% per line, "
+          f"baseline: {baseline_path})")
+    print(fmt_table(manifest))
+    if shrank:
+        print(f"improvements: {len(shrank)} line(s) shrank, "
+              f"{len(removed)} line(s) removed")
+        for name, old, cur in shrank[:10]:
+            print(f"  shrank  {name}  {old} -> {cur}")
+        for name, old in removed[:10]:
+            print(f"  removed {name}  ({old} bytes)")
+    if failures:
+        print(f"::error::size budget regression in {artifact} "
+              f"({len(failures)} line(s) beyond +{budget_pct}%):")
+        for f in failures:
+            print(f)
+        print("intentional growth? re-seed with: python3 scripts/size_manifest.py "
+              f"check <artifact> --baseline {baseline_path} --init-if-missing")
+        return 1
+    print(f"size budget OK (TOTAL {total_pct:+.1f}% vs baseline)")
+    return 0
+
+
+def selftest() -> int:
+    """Synthetic-artifact assertions; exits nonzero on any failure."""
+    import tempfile
+    import os
+
+    ok = True
+
+    def expect(label, actual, wanted):
+        nonlocal ok
+        status = "ok" if actual == wanted else "FAIL"
+        if actual != wanted:
+            ok = False
+        print(f"  [{status}] {label}: exit {actual} (want {wanted})")
+
+    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:
+        td = Path(td)
+
+        def make_zip(path: Path, a_size: int, extra: "dict[str, int] | None" = None):
+            with zipfile.ZipFile(path, "w") as zf:
+                zf.writestr("bin/a.bin", b"\0" * a_size)
+                zf.writestr("bin/b.bin", b"\0" * (10 * 1024))
+                for name, size in (extra or {}).items():
+                    zf.writestr(name, b"\0" * size)
+
+        base_zip, cur_zip = td / "base.zip", td / "cur.zip"
+        make_zip(base_zip, 100 * 1024)
+        make_zip(cur_zip, 100 * 1024)
+        base = td / "base.tsv"
+        r = check(cur_zip, base, 5.0, True, None)
+        expect("init-if-missing seeds + passes", r, 0)
+
+        make_zip(cur_zip, 104 * 1024)  # +4%: within budget
+      …

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`
  (four modes — `sequence` equal-width slots, `duration` with idle gaps
  compressed out, `time` zero-width wall-clock markers, `actual` real gaps;
  three fixed lanes: 0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools),
  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),
  and `ThrottledTrajectorySearchIndex` (full-text; matches are stable
  record ids). `formatters.dart` holds the shared duration/token/throughput
  formatting; `trajectory_preview.dart` the bounded single-line previews;
  `trajectory_export.dart` the whole-snapshot JSON/Markdown exporters the
  header's copy menu uses. Tool records carry `startedAt` (real launch
  time, distinct from the projected position) so the Gantt/actual
  projections plot true spans. Outbound model requests persist for the
  ledger …
